text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — router tail latency spike detected in eu-west-2 (p99 > SLO). Paging SRE oncall and routing owners. bridge: https://call.redwood/bridge/3301234567 :rotating_light:
emily: on it, grabbing logs and perf dashboard. any recent deploys to routing or lb policy?
lucas: I rolled a routing-weight policy at 08:42 UTC to reduce cross-zone traffic; version v2.3.7. leaving it in canary (5%) but canary expanded to 25% via autoscaler rule earlier.
raj: i'm oncall, joining bridge. can someone post p95/p99 numbers?
alice: customer telemetry: streaming stall alerts from two high-traffic customers in eu-west-2. session drop/reconnects align with ~08:55-09:10 UTC.
emily: dashboards: p95 from ~120ms -> 450ms, p99 from 1.2s -> 6.8s for router egress in eu-west-2. streaming stall ratio jumped 0.02% -> 1.6%.
kevin: infra telemetry shows a handful of backends with 95-99% CPU on GPU hosts and elevated queue lengths. heatmap attached in dashboard (link).
lucas: looking at router logs: seeing repeated ejections and then reassigns to same hot shard. snippet:
```
[router] time=2026-03-15T09:02:13Z policy=weight_canary shard=hot-42 chosen_backend=shard-A load=0.98 reassign_count=12
[router] time=2026-03-15T09:02:14Z policy=weight_canary shard=hot-42 chosen_backend=shard-A load=0.99 kv_cache_miss=true streaming_chunk_delay=800ms
```
emily: that looks like a hot-partition getting pinned to a backend, KV cache misses + heavy load -> streaming stalls and tail latency. why is policy picking same backend repeatedly?
lucas: suspect a bug in fallback routing where zone affinity weights get zeroed for certain keys, causing weight normalization to concentrate traffic. i have a local repro.
raj: customer impact: which customers affected and scope? alice?
alice: two enterprise customers reported degraded streaming sessions (~1200 sessions impacted across accounts). no data loss, but service disruption and aborted sessions. estimated outage window 08:55-09:10 UTC.
emily: immediate mitigation options: 1) scale up pool for shard-A, 2) force rollback of canary policy, 3) apply per-key jitter to break hot-loop, 4) activate warm-fallback routing to replica pool. which is fastest?
kevin: quickest is rolling back canary to previous stable policy (v2.3.6) and enabling warm-fallback. scaling GPU pool may take too long (~10-15m).
lucas: rollback command ready: `rctl rollout routing-policy --namespace=eu-west-2 --to-version=v2.3.6 --expedite`
raj: do it. emily, can you coordinate the rollback and monitor p99? i'll watch customer telemetry and handle comms.
emily: executing rollback now. pasting output:
```
$ rctl rollout routing-policy --namespace=eu-west-2 --to-version=v2.3.6 --expedite
Rolling back canary -> v2.3.6
Applying config to 25% of routers... done
Verifying... OK
```
emily: enabling warm-fallback routing flag for eu-west-2: `feature_flags.routing.warm_fallback = true`
kevin: warm-fallback applied, dispatching traffic to replica pool with lower load. also bumping ejection thresholds to avoid oscillation while we stabilize.
alice: customer comms: posted initial status update to affected accounts, flagged that we are mitigating and will follow up with RCA.
emily: p95 now down to 160ms, p99 falling: 6.8s -> 2.1s within 90s of rollback. streaming stall ratio trending down to 0.3%.
raj: good. keep monitoring for 15m. open incident bridge and start incident timeline.
emily: bridge is up. adding timeline entry: "09:02 detect p99 spike; 09:06 rollback policy; 09:08 enable warm-fallback; 09:10 p99 trending down."
lucas: i'm collecting repro details and will open a bug on routing weight normalization. preliminary root cause: canary expansion logic didn't account for zeroing zone-affinity weight on overflow keys -> weight mass collapses to few backends.
kevin: putting a temporary alert rule to catch rapid ejection/reassign cycles: `alert: RapidRouterReassigns` threshold: >5 reassigns/min for same shard.
raj: assign action items: lucas -> bug + patch (priority P0), emily -> postmortem with timeline and customer impact, kevin -> reclaim warm-fallback flag clean removal plan, alice -> follow up comms to customers with ETA for RCA. i'll stay oncall until handoff.
pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by raj. escalation: paged EMs for routing and infra.
emily: any outstanding customer errors or new reports?
alice: one new minor report at 09:12 but reconnect succeeded after 2 retries. no new major incidents.
raj: planning handoff in 30 min to next oncall (sre-rotation). leaving notes in bridge. anyone else to add?
lucas: I'll push a hotfix branch to prevent zeroing zone affinity and add unit tests. will also add a canary safety check to prevent >20% expansion without manual ack.
kevin: I'll document rollback playbook steps and add a faster path in console for emergency policy rollback.
emily: thanks team. postmortem assigned and will include mitigations: stricter canary expansion caps, better ejection alerts, and permanent warm-fallback defaults for streaming traffic.
raj: closing active page. monitoring until 09:45 then will hand off. good job. :thumbsup:
